header: L3 · The maintainer three years from now · sonnet
verdict: L3-R10-3 reads as resolved (the overlap sentence is in 05 5.3). L3-R10-1 and L3-R10-2 are parked for stage B (P1, P2), not re-reported. The delta adds one Required defect (the import closure of the pr package cannot hold as written) and two Advisory ones.

findings.section: 05 5.3 (approvals globs, the pr package paragraph); 12 12.4 (approvalLine in tools/ci/askfirst.go); 10 10.7
findings.defect: The closure rule says pr, a main package at tools/ci/pr, imports only the standard library and 'paths on approvals', but the approvals globs name files (tools/ci/askfirst.go, tools/ci/denylist.yaml), and askfirst.go sits in the main package tools/ci, which no other package can import. go list -deps lists packages, not files, so the test has no defined comparison. The shared code pr needs (approvalLine, the grants reader, git handling) has no importable home inside the closure.
findings.scenario: At T005 the implementer finds approvalLine cannot be imported from tools/ci/askfirst.go, and either copies it (two approval grammars that drift) or moves it to a package such as internal/askfirst, which is outside the globs, so the go list -deps test fails or is loosened with a glob nobody approved. The ask-first globs then grow by hand, the drift this closure was meant to stop.
findings.change: State the home of the shared code as a package (for example tools/ci/pr/internal/..., or one package tools/ci/askfirst), put its glob on approvals, say that the test compares package directories with the globs, and move approvalLine's location in 12 12.4 to match. Add the tools/ci/pr package to 10.7 or say that 10.7 does not govern it.

findings.defect: The one command listing still gives `go run ./tools/ci pr <payload file>` and `go run ./tools/ci pr --title <t> --body <file>`, while 10 10.2 and 12 12.4 now run `go run ./tools/ci/pr`. Only a shorthand sentence in 12 12.4 reconciles `tools/ci pr` (used in about thirty places) with the package.
findings.scenario: A maintainer or agent copies the 12.2 command, which no longer exists, or greps the spec for the invocation and finds two spellings for one program.
findings.change: Change the two lines in 12.2 to ./tools/ci/pr, and either keep the shorthand with a Vocabulary entry or write the package path where the command is meant.

findings.defect: Import boundaries now have two enforcers: `tools/ci imports` over internal/ (10.7) and a separate `go list -deps` test for tools/ci/pr, with 10.7 and the imports row silent about the second.
findings.scenario: A reader of 10.7 treats it as the whole boundary list; a later agent adds a package rule in one place and not the other.
findings.change: Fold the pr closure rule into `tools/ci imports` as a row of 10.7, or name the test in the imports row of 10.2 so there is one list.
